scope: Prior prepared mixes; one LibriSpeech narration mixed with fan, keyboard, and rain at 5 dB SNR. Not the new real-call clips.
metric: Extended STOI, higher is better; pystoi(clean, output, 48000, extended=True). Same 10-second window including its padded pauses.
export_check: Base Core ML PCM16 outputs matched the PyTorch checkpoint within 3.08e-5 maximum absolute sample error on the first 9.9 seconds of each clip, consistent with PCM16 quantization.
conclusion: DeepFilterNet3 has higher eSTOI than Base in all three prepared mixes. Reducing Base to 70% does not consistently improve eSTOI. The current Base checkpoint is not established as the best listening-quality option.
limits: Three constructed examples from one speaker are not a general benchmark.
eSTOI measures predicted intelligibility, not naturalness or listening preference.
A clean speech reference is unavailable for the new real-world recordings; no intrusive score is assigned to those excerpts.
Human listening review and independent broader evaluation remain necessary.
